about: Hand-drawn truth for the page scan (reflow.extract.scan) on the working copies OCR writes (#82: redo keeps a page's image objects and visible text; force, for outlines and unreadable visible text, leaves one raster). Boxes are page points, top-left origin. 'pictures': every box must be matched by a picture region at IoU >= 0.8, and an empty list means no picture region. 'text_only': the scan finds no region at all. 'rules': each box must be overlapped by a rule region. 'pen': the scan finds pen ink (true) or none (false). 'objects': the kind of every image object, in page order. 'pen_boxes': the writing OCR cannot read, hand-drawn; each must be matched by a pen region at IoU >= 0.5. 'pen_missed': writing the scan misses today, each matched by no pen region (a strict xfail: move a box to pen_boxes once it is found). 'typed': typed text, which no pen region may overlap (#84).

pages.note: Five cover photos set as one collage under the title, on a blue page. Redo keeps the page image, the title's mask (text), the logo and the small masks of the sign's digits and the truck (plain).
Born-digital text page: no image object, nothing rendered.
A river photo above a typed letter. Redo keeps the page image, the letter's own image (text) and three small masks in the photo.

A black-and-white photo above a drawn timeline. The timeline is a flat-colour graphic whose labels OCR reads; only its row of circles has texture, so it is not boxed here. Two of its label lines ('Treatment facilities;', 'filling Del'), which OCR garbled and #83 left out, are pen: ink no text explains, inside the timeline's image object, whose own ink they stay.

Signature page: the signatures are pen ink. #82 keeps the file's own OCR layer; #147 grades it, so the secretary's blue signature is no longer masked. Its strokes are two clusters on one line, joined into one region (#257).
Affidavit of publication with a signature and a notary stamp.
A typed tax form with vector rules and a small signature.

Born-digital letter sliced into eight image strips under a live text layer. The letterhead strip (logo and address, no text layer of its own) is text once redo OCR reads its address, and its logo is the one picture; the strip under it holds the live heading; the last strip holds the footer rule and the live folio 'iii', so it is text, and with the rule left out it has no ink.
Two typed sections under a header rule 496 pt wide.
A printed cemetery map with its labels (CROSBY, Gletzen); no handwriting.
A hand-drawn map of the cemetery plots, lettered with the street names.

A worksheet answered in purple pen. #82 keeps the file's own OCR layer; #147 grades it, so its readings of the handwriting are unread and the pen is found. The large answers were found in pieces, a region per cluster of working (#257): the clusters on one line, and the lines that touch, are joined. The second question's answer line stays missed: its left half, 'NaC2H3O2', is purple pen whose tiles are dense enough (0.5 against DENSE_MARK 0.4) to be dropped as a solid mark, so no pen region covers it and the right half is under half of the box. The third typed line ends in handwriting, so only its typed start is a typed box.
A handwritten ledger under a printed header row: pen, not a picture.

The ledger continued: handwriting under the printed header row. #147 grades the kept OCR layer, so its word 'Mot-o,._', read in the handwriting, masks by its box; its pad cuts the ledger's bottom rule in the last strip into pieces too short for a rule, so that strip is plain, far under a figure's size.

A typed report cover. The red MIT library stamp is pen colour that no text reads. The purple 'AERO. & ASTRO. LIBRARY' stamp, of which Tesseract reads nothing, is pen colour too (#147). The blue handwritten 'Copy #3' is missed: #147 drops the kept layer's reading of it ("6'17 #i 5"), but its faint pencil is too little ink for a region and its inked '#3' is a solid mark.
